findings.text: Locked TD vCPU command service validates protection key assignment and pre-runnable TD state then serves CPUID query and rejects other selectors.

Unlocked TD vCPU command service ingests a user command, holds VM state protection, validates assignment and pre-runnable state, brackets dispatch with vCPU load handling, and serves memory seeding and vCPU creation while reporting unknown selectors distinctly.
TDX guest memory mapping cap leaves shared pages unpromoted and limits private pages to small pages.
Locked memory encryption dispatch accepts only TD vCPUs and forwards to the TDX locked handler.
Unlocked memory encryption dispatch accepts only TD vCPUs and forwards to the TDX unlocked handler.
Mapping level dispatch selects TDX limits for TD guests and a default level otherwise.

Module init brings up VMX first, sizes the shared vCPU cache as the larger of VMX and TDX layouts when TDX is enabled, advertises the TDX VM type, exposes the device only after common init, and unwinds VMX on failure.
Module teardown leaves common KVM then VMX, with VMX teardown clearing the small physical address allowance and restoring L1D mitigation while releasing the flush buffer when present.
User command intake requires successful ingestion and a clear hardware error field on entry because that field is reserved for host to user reporting.

TD finalize requires an assigned key and a not yet runnable TD, surfaces module busy separately from internal failure, and on success marks TD_STATE_RUNNABLE before enabling pre-fault with an ordering barrier.

vCPU creation requires empty flags and VCPU_TD_STATE_UNINITIALIZED, enforces an x2APIC base with bootstrap handling, initializes the hardware vCPU, programs posted interrupt delivery, then records VCPU_TD_STATE_INITIALIZED.

Memory seeding requires VCPU_TD_STATE_INITIALIZED in a non-runnable TD, allows only the measurement flag, and validates page alignment, nonzero source, nonempty count, address wraparound, and private coverage of both first and last byte.

CPUID metadata access bounds subleaf width and total entries, rejects unreadable leaf patterns, derives identifiers from leaf high bit and low bits plus subleaf presence, reads value halves as a pair, and corrects phys width for the extended address size leaf.

CPUID enumeration discovers the normal maximum then walks that range and discovers the extended maximum then walks that range, reports sizing failure while still returning the needed count when the user buffer is small, and distinguishes user faults from hardware read failures.
Leaf collection first probes without subleaf significance and only on hardware read failure walks subleaves until failure, succeeding when at least one subleaf read worked.
TD init maps entropy exhaustion to a retryable error, user-caused invalid operands to an invalid error while preserving the hardware code for diagnosis, and internal module failures to an I/O error.

Hardware vCPU bring-up allocates a backing page plus a control page array, creates the vCPU object, attaches each control page, performs hardware init with caller context and vCPU identifier, then marks KVM_MP_STATE_RUNNABLE.
Hardware vCPU init holds the MMU lock for write across the init call to match exclusive resource use inside the module and to let concurrent no-fail invalidations succeed.
Unlocked vCPU commands serialize against VM state with a validated scoped guard and bracket hardware access with vCPU load and release.
TD moves from unassigned to assigned to TD_STATE_RUNNABLE, with CPUID query, unlocked creation, memory seeding, and finalize all rejected once runnable.
TD vCPU moves from VCPU_TD_STATE_UNINITIALIZED to VCPU_TD_STATE_INITIALIZED via creation and then to scheduler runnable via hardware init, with memory seeding permitted only while initialized.
Command envelope carries an operation selector, modifier flags, a user pointer payload, and a hardware error output that userspace must leave clear.
Memory seeding descriptor carries source address, guest address, and remaining page count, and is written back to reflect consumed progress even on interruption or failure.

Virtualization operation tables select between VT and VMX handlers through selector macros, with TDX-only slots resolving to VT handlers when enabled and to null otherwise, and init operations bind hardware setup plus runtime, PMU, and nesting tables.
Command identifiers KVM_TDX_GET_CPUID, KVM_TDX_INIT_MEM_REGION, and KVM_TDX_INIT_VCPU select distinct operations, with KVM_TDX_MEASURE_MEMORY_REGION requesting measurement during seeding.
VT requires a fixed APICV inhibit set combining disabled, absent, hypervisor, block IRQ, physical ID alias, APIC ID change, and APIC base change reasons.
CPUID handling observes KVM_MAX_CPUID_ENTRIES, marks subleaf-significant entries with KVM_CPUID_FLAG_SIGNIFCANT_INDEX, and special-cases leaf 0x80000008 for phys bits correction.
Posted interrupt setup programs POSTED_INTR_NV with POSTED_INTR_VECTOR, POSTED_INTR_DESC_ADDR from the per-vCPU descriptor, and PIN_BASED_POSTED_INTR in PIN_BASED_VM_EXEC_CONTROL.
Execution control read helper reports hardware failure only via a log and a zero value, so callers cannot distinguish failure from legitimate zero.
CPUID value halves are read as consecutive fields where failure of the first half clears the entry and returns an I/O error while failure of only the second half is treated as unexpected.
Seeding iterates one page at a time with signal checks and rescheduling, preserves partial progress on interruption, but failure to write back progress overrides the loop status.
TD init failure after partial control attachment frees only the not yet attached tail from the current index and relies on full key release plus control reclaim to tolerate partial state.
Control page attachment failure splits ownership so already attached pages are left for vCPU teardown while remaining pages are freed locally and nulled.
TDCS_EXEC lifts a small field number into the module field namespace for the execution controls class.
Single-argument bug checker extends the common checker by reporting the callee name plus one caller value in hexadecimal.
Metadata field read is a direct pass-through to the management read primitive that returns hardware status unchanged.
L1D flush teardown releases the flush buffer when allocated and always restores mitigation to automatic.
